I will keep things simple and familiar. In Quzhou County, the safest choice for me is still the usual winter wheat and summer maize rotation. I am 70 years old, so I do not want a complicated mix of crops that needs too much extra labor, marketing, or hand work. Wheat and maize fit my land, my experience, and the local water and machinery conditions. I will use improved seed, not expensive specialty crops, because I want stable production more than risk. I will fertilize enough to secure yield, but not push too hard, because fertilizer costs money and too much can waste water and burn the crop. I will irrigate wheat more than maize, since wheat in our area depends more on timely water, especially at key stages. I will use rotary tillage because it is easier and faster for me to manage than deeper ploughing every season. I will spray only as needed for the common diseases, insects, and weeds, keeping the number of applications moderate. My goal is steady grain, manageable work, and lower risk through the full year.
